notes: The site has no dedicated services page; services come from the homepage 'What we do' section. The showcased work is mostly enterprise tech / B2B (Google, AWS, CrowdStrike, Salesforce, Meta), plus financial services (AIG, J.P. Morgan), HR (ADP), energy (Renew Home) and science philanthropy (Simons Foundation). p5 is deliberately outside all of these.

personas.label: Startup security PMM
personas.marketing_problem: They're launching a second product that creates a new sub-category. Analysts and buyers don't get the platform story, sales decks are inconsistent, and a much larger competitor owns the category language.
personas.articulateness: high: uses PMM vocabulary (positioning, marketecture, ICP, GTM, messaging house)
personas.win: A positioning and messaging framework, plus a marketecture visual that sales actually uses, ready in time for their RSA Conference launch.

personas.label: Fortune 100 financial-services comms VP
personas.marketing_problem: After a restructuring, the company has to re-introduce itself to institutional clients and brokers, and the CEO has a high-stakes investor-day keynote in five months. Internal stakeholders and legal slow everything down.
personas.articulateness: high: polished, executive and risk-averse; asks about process, governance and senior-level experience
personas.win: A credible repositioning narrative the board signs off on, and a CEO keynote that lands with analysts without creating legal exposure.

personas.label: Big-tech partner marketing lead
personas.company_type: Large enterprise cloud / productivity software company
personas.marketing_problem: They need to scale co-marketing across hundreds of partners: enablement kits, co-branded video, a virtual partner summit, and customer stories. Their in-house team is stretched and output is inconsistent.
personas.articulateness: medium: busy and practical; writes short multi-part asks about capacity, speed and repeatable templates
personas.win: A repeatable partner-marketing system (templates, video, an event) that partners actually use, and that they can show pipeline influence from.
likely_relevant_work: Android: Crafting a Brand New Virtual Event

personas.label: Science foundation comms director
personas.company_size: ~250 staff, grant-making plus in-house research institutes
personas.marketing_problem: Their brand looks dated and fragmented across programs. They need to explain basic research to the public, to policymakers and to prospective scientists, and they're launching a new education initiative.
personas.technical_level: low on marketing, high on subject matter
personas.articulateness: high: thoughtful, long-form; wary of 'marketing speak'; asks about values and audience understanding
personas.win: A unified brand identity and content approach that makes the science approachable without dumbing it down, and that internal researchers respect.
personas.site_alignment: edge: one showcased client (Simons Foundation), otherwise thin coverage
likely_relevant_work: Simons Foundation: Illuminating a New Brand Identity
Google Cloud: Illuminating a New Brand Identity

personas.label: Regional restaurant group owner (out of domain)
personas.marketing_problem: Weeknight foot traffic is down, a new chain is opening nearby, and they want Instagram/TikTok content, a better website with online ordering, and a local launch event for a fifth location. Budget is small.
personas.articulateness: low: short, informal, sometimes vague messages; asks about price early
personas.win: More covers on weeknights and a busy opening for the new location, on a budget they can afford.
personas.site_alignment: outside: no hospitality, restaurant, local-business or small-budget consumer work on the site. Use this persona to test the fallback and whether the model forces irrelevant enterprise tech case studies onto it.
